en: As the user of an agent, you may also have
some ways of passing extra instructions,
though that depends on how the agent was
built. For example, Claude Cowork will look
for a file named Claude MD in any folder you
added to a project and you're working in
and load that file automatically into the
agent context window
and therefore follow or consider any
instructions or information you have in that
Claude MD file. So for example, in this
Claude MD file, Claude Data Analysis folder,
which I loaded, which you find attached,
there is a Claude MD file.
And if I open that with a text editor, in
that file are some general instructions on
how I want an AI agent to perform data
analysis
and how it should create a report when asked
for it.
This is just something I made up for this
demo, but that's the kind of information you
could put into that file when working with
Claude. Claude Cowork or Claude Code.
Most other agents support a similar concept.
Claude Cowork and Claude Code are kind of
the exceptions, to be honest, because most
other agents will look for an agents.md
file, which then serves the same purpose
though.
The idea behind these files is basically
that they act as a README for agents so that
agents will automatically discover and load
them. And most agents even discover nested
files. So if you had a folder loaded into an
agent that had this shape and it had a
subfolder with its own agents.md file,
most agents would also consider this file
when working in that subfolder of the loaded
folder and this file in general whenever
doing any work inside of that folder.
And again, the idea is simply that you have
a place to put your instructions as plain
Markdown for agents to consider them.
And of course, not just instructions, but
also any other kind of core context or
information you want to give to your agent.
And Claude MD, just to be clear, is exactly
the same concept just for Claude Code and
Claude Cowork.
You typically want to have one of the two,
or if you are indeed frequently switching
between those different agents, like maybe
you use ChatGPT and sometimes also Claude
Cowork, you could simply mirror or link
these files together. And many agents will
respect that standard and will load AgentsMD
or ClaudeMD. And that is very important. As
the developer of an agent, you actively have
to decide whether you want to support that
standard and you want your agent to search
for AgentsMD or ClaudeMD files and load them
or not. It's not a magical functionality
that's automatically given.
For example, here I have a task-specific
agent in code, and again, We'll dive into
that later. And you also don't need to be a
programmer. That's not the focus here.
But I have an agent in code here. And in
that code, I'm never searching for Agents.md
files or Claude.md files. This basic agent
here, this very basic task-specific agent
does not support this feature. But many
agents, especially the general agents, do.
And that's therefore then one way for you as
the user to also provide some instructions
to an agent. Instructions that will
automatically be loaded into every context
window whenever you start a new session and
that session has access to a folder that
includes an Agents.md or Claude.md file.
